MINISTRY OF DRINKING WATER AND SANITATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3486 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 23.03.2017 
 
Implementation of NRDWP 
 
3486. SHRI Y.V. SUBBA REDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of DRINKING WATER AND SANITATION be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether implementation of National Rural Drink ing Water Programme (NRDWP) in Andhra 
Pradesh was reviewed recently;  
(b)  if so, the details and the outcome thereof; 
(c)  whether there are still more than 2600 habitat ions where quality of water has been affected 
and in more than 25,000 habitations drinking water is partially covered in the State; and 
 (d)  the steps being taken by the Union Government  to supplement the efforts of the State 
Government to achieve the target to cover the above  habitations and also to improve water 
quality?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR DRINKING WATER AND SANITATION 
(SHRI RAMESH CHANDAPPA JIGAJINAGI) 
(a)& (b) Providing drinking water supply to the rur al population is a dynamic and continuous 
process. This Ministry assists states for improving  the coverage of safe drinking water in rural 
areas through National Rural Drinking Water Program me (NRDWP) and under which State 
Governments are competent to plan, design, approve and implement rural drinking water supply 
schemes. The physical & financial progress of NRDWP is monitored & reviewed through National 
/ State level review meetings, conferences and vide o-conferences. A National Level Review 
Meeting with Secretaries of State Governments for R ural Drinking Water Supply Departments 
including Andhra Pradesh was held under the chairma nship of Secretary, Ministry of Drinking 
Water & Sanitation, Government of India on Septembe r 9-10 th , 2016. Further, performance / 
progress of Andhra Pradesh was reviewed during Annu al Action Plan (AAP) meeting on 
01.03.2017 by the Ministry officials. 
 
(c) No Madam. As per data entered by the State Gove rnment of Andhra Pradesh on Integrated 
Management Information System (IMIS) of this Minist ry, as on 19.03.2017, there are 517 quality 
affected habitations (i.e. containing at least one chemical contaminant) and 14,775 habitations 
Partially Covered habitations (i.e. getting less th an 40 litre per capita per day safe drinking water)  
in the State of Andhra Pradesh.

state of Andhra Pradesh under NRDWP.

ongoing schemes covering Arsenic / Fluoride affecte d habitations, Rs. 11.83 lakh has been

MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
LOK SABHA

TO BE ANSWERED ON 23.03.2017 
 
EXCHANGE OF TECHNOLOGY 
 
3487.   SHRI ARVIND SAWANT: 
 
Will the Minister of NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Union Government proposes to exchange technology with other countries to improve the 
electricity generation capacity through new and renewable energy sources and to reduce the production cost 
thereof;   
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the other measures taken or likely to be taken by the Union Government to develop affordable new and 
renewable energy sources in the country? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR POWER, COAL, NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND MINES 
(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) (SHRI PIYUSH GOYAL) 
 
(a) & (b): Yes Madam. Government of India through Ministry of New and Renewable Energy  (MNRE) 
have MoUs containing details regarding exchange of technologies with number of countries on numerous 
subjects including improving the  electricity generation c apacity and to reduce the production cost. Details of 
countries having MoUs with India on exchange of technology is given at Annexure –I.  
 
(c): The steps taken by the  Government to increase the generation of renewable energy sources viz wind 
energy, solar energy, biomass and small hydro power includes:  
 Incentives in the forms of generation based incentives/subsidies, fiscal incentives such as accelerated 
depreciation, concessional customs duty, excise duty exemptions, income tax holiday for 10 years and 
viability gap funding from NCEF. 
 Up-scaling of the target of renewable energy capacity to 175 GW by the year 2022 which includes 100 
GW from solar, 60 GW from wind, 10 GW from bio-power and 5 GW from small hydro-power; 
 amendments in the Tariff Policy for s trong enforcement of Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) and 
for providing Renewable Generation Obligation (RGO);  
 setting up of exclusive solar parks;  
 development of power transmission network through Green Energy Corridor project;  
 identification of large government complexes/ buildings for rooftop projects;  
 infrastructure status for solar projects;  
 raising tax free solar bonds;  
 making roof top solar a part of housing loan by banks/NHB;  
 incorporating measures in Integrated Power Development Scheme (I PDS) for encouraging distribution 
companies and making net-metering compulsory;  

 raising funds from bilateral and international donors as also from the Green Climate Fund to achieve the 
target. and  
 creation of Surya Mitras for installation and maintenance of the Solar Projects.

MOU WITH PORTUGAL FOR COOPERATION IN CLEAN ENERGY

Will the Minister of NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has recently signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) 
with Portugal for co-operation in clean energy;   
(b) if so, the details thereof; and

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS
(DEPARTMENT OF SPORTS)
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3498
TO BE ANSWERED ON 23/3/2017
Financial Assistance to Sportspersons
+3498.  SHRI KUNWAR PUSHPENDRA SINGH CHANDEL:
    SHRI DEVJI M. PATEL:
    SHRI GOPAL SHETTY:
             SHRI DILIPKUMAR MANSUKHLAL GANDHI
          
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to
state: 
(a) the  details  of  schemes  under  which  financial  assistance  for
promotion of various sports is provided by the Government;
(b) whether  the  Government  provides  cash  incentives  to
sportspersons  under  various  sports  disciplines  to  encourage
their participation and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has any provisions of providing sports
equipments to the sportspersons and if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether the Government has taken note of alleged irregularities
in  the  utilization  of  financial  assistance  released  by  the
Government for the sportspersons during the last three years and
the current year;
(e) if  so, the action taken by the Government against those held
responsible for such irregularities; and

(f) the  steps  taken/being  taken  by  the  Government  to  prevent
recurrence of such irregularities in future?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR YOUTH
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS
(SHRI VIJAY GOEL)
(a) to (c) Madam,  ‘Sports’  is  a  State  subject.  Promotion  &
development of various sports disciplines is the primary responsibility
of  the  State  Government/  National  Sports  Federations  (NSFs).  The
Government supplements the efforts of the State Governments/ NSFs
by providing financial assistance under the following schemes:- 
 1. Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs):- Under the  
Scheme  grants  are  provided  to  the  recognized  NSFs  for  
organizing  National/International  tournaments  in  India,  
participation  of  National  team/athletes  in  the  international  
competitions abroad, coaching/training of national team/athletes 
in India and abroad, engagement of foreign coaches, equipment 
support etc.  
To promote sports in the country, Sports Authority of India 
(SAI)  is  also  implementing  the  following  sports  promotion  
schemes to identify talented sports persons in the age groups at 
national and international competitions:
 National Sports Talent Contest Scheme (NSTC)
 Army Boys Sports company (ABSC)
 SAI Training Center (STC)
 Special Area Games (SAG)
 Extension Centers of STC/SAG
 Center of Excellence (COE)
 National Sports Academy (NSA) 
Accordingly, SAI has established 10 Regional Centers and 02  
educational  institutions  to  implement  the  above  sports  
promotions  schemes  in  the  country  through  273  SAI  sports  
centers.

2. Scheme of National Sports Development Fund(NSDF):- Identified 
probable  athletes  and  selected  elite  athletes  are  provided  
financial  assistance  under  the  Target  Olympic  Podium  (TOP)  
Scheme under the National Sports Development Fund with the  
objective of identifying and supporting potential medal prospects
for Olympic games.
3. Khelo India – National Programme for Development of Sports:-
The  Government  has  launched  a  new  Central  Sector  Scheme
namely ‘Khelo India – National Programme for Development of
Sports’ to spot talent through countrywide competitions, to train
and groom the talent and to provide sporting infrastructure for
honing the sporting skills for implementation from the financial
year  2016-17  onwards.  This  Scheme  provides  for  holding  of
sports competitions in two age groups of  (i) under 14 and (ii)
under 17 all over India to encourage mass participation of both
boys and girls in Sports in both urban and rural areas, sports
talent  identification  and  creatin  of  sports  infrastructure
facilities,  namely,  Synthetic  Athletic  Track,  Synthetic  Hockey
field,  Synthetic  Turf  Football  Ground,  Multipurpose  hall,
Swimming pool and construction of stadia complex. 
4. Scheme of Incentives to Sports Persons:- 
Under the scheme of  special awards to medal winners in
international sports events and their coaches, cash awards are
given to sportspersons and coaches. Besides, Government also
confers the following awards with award money on distinguished
players & coaches. :-
Name of Award Award money 
1. Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award Rs. 7.5 Lakh
2. Arjuna Award RS. 5.0 Lakh
3. Dhyanchand Awards RS. 5.0 Lakh
4. Dronacharya Award RS. 5.0 Lakh
5. National Welfare Fund for sportspersons:- 
Under the scheme financial assistance is provided to outstanding
sportspersons of  yesteryears, living in indigent circumstances who

had  brought  glory  to  the  country  in  sports.  Lump  sum  ex-gratia
assistance is given to the sportspersons or their families for medical
treatment etc. 
6.  Scheme of Sports Fund for Pension to Meritorious Sportspersons:- 
Under this scheme, those sportspersons who are Indian citizens
and have won gold, silver and bronze medals in Olympic Games, World
Cup/world championships  Asian  Games, Commonwealth Games  and
Paralympic  Games  and  have  retired  from  active  sports  career  are
eligible for life pension.
(d) to (f) No  such  incident has  been  reported.  In  order  to  ensure
proper utilization of Government grants released to NSFs, the Ministry
insists on submission of utilization certificates and audited accounts.
Balance grant and future grants for an event is released only after
settlement of accounts for the previous grant.  Moreover, the accounts
of NSFs are to be audited by the Chartered Accountants in the Panel
of Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG). Also, the accounts
of the NSFs receiving Government grant exceeding Rs 1.00 crore are
subject to audit from the CAG.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES, 
RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3499 
ANSWERED ON 23.03.2017 
 
CLEANING OF YAMUNA RIVER 
 
3499.       SHRI C.N. JAYADEVAN 
 
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA 
REJUVENATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that water quality of Yamuna river has not improved even 
after spending about Rs.2000 crores on its cleaning and if so, the details/facts thereof and the 
reasons therefor;  
(b) the details of various projects implemented/being implemented to clean-up the river; and  
(c) the time by which the river is to be made pollution free along with the further efforts to be 
made to clean it? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) FOR YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS AND MINISTER OF 
STATE FOR WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA 
REJUVENATION  
(SHRI VIJAY GOEL) 
(a) to (c)  Cleaning of Rivers is an ongoing process and this Ministry is supplementing the 
efforts of the States for pollution abatement of river Yamuna, a tributary of River Ganga, by 
providing financial assistance to States of Haryana,  Delhi and Uttar Pradesh in phased manner 
since 1993 under the Yamuna Action Plan (YAP). Works taken up relate to 
sewerage/interception and diversion of drains, sewage treatment plants (STPs), low cost 
sanitation/community toilet complexes, electric/improved wood crematoria, etc.  
Till date under Yamuna Action Plans, 942.25 mld STP capacity has been created and 
rehabilitation and upgradation of 950 MLD of existing STP capacity is in process. Further, 
under NRCP, two projects, were sanctioned in Sonepat and Panipat for pollution abatement in 
Sonepat and Panipat to create 70 mld of new STP and rehabilitation of 75 MLD STP capacity. 
In addition, under Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) project of 
Ministry of Urban Development (MoUD), an interceptor sewer project costing Rs. 1357 crore is 
being implemented by Delhi Jal Board (DJB) to intercept sewage flowing into river Yamuna 
from three major drains, namely , Najafgarh, Supplementary and Shahdara in Delhi. Visible 
improvement in quality of river Yamuna is expected after completion of ongoing projects.
